newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise on revived investor interest.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise on revived investor interest.

text.p: Jordanian stocks rose on Sunday, buoyed by revived investor interest in select stock led by market leader Arab Bank, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.39 percent to 145.96 points from 145.38 points on Saturday, the start of weekly trade.
A total of 561,374 shares changed hands on Sunday in healthy 989,817 dinar turnover.

Dealers attributed high volume of trade to some bloc sales including sustained activity on key stock, Arab Bank, -- a quarter of value traded -- Livestock and Poultry and Jordan Electric Power with high earnings prospect.
Of 53 stocks traded, 27 advanced, 15 fell and 11 were unchanged. Six posted year lows.

Dealers said unfaltering demand on Arab Bank, a major component of the index, for the second week was still underpinned by expectations of a bonus share once a new companies law is passed before the end of the year.
"There was an improvement in turnover with some bloc sales and continued demand on key stock that helped cushion prices," one broker said.

Investment sentiment has picked up slightly since the government announced last month a package of economic reforms in the wake of recent unrest fuelled by the government's doubling of bread prices in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- rose 0.02 percent to 81.18 points. It was 15.00 percent down on last year.
In industrials, the leading sector, Livestock and Poultry again dominated activity with another 20 fils rise to 680 fils on a moderately high 122,966 dinar turnover.

Jordan Cement Factories, a focus of foreign investor interest, rose 10 fils to 3.340 dinars. Universal Modern Industries shed 40 fils to 1.740 dinars. Jordan Petroleum Refinery shed 20 fils to 9.260 dinars.

In banks, aside from market leader Arab Bank's turnover, most stock saw minimal activity with the exception of a large bloc sale in Middle East Investment Bank. Debt-ridden Amman Investment Bank, currently in Central Bank sanctioned negotiations with the Arab Bank over a buyout, rose 10 fils to 230 fils. Islamic Bank rose 30 fils to 3.640 dinars.
In services, Jordan Electric Power rose 40 fils to 1.660 dinars after 81,178 shares changed hands. National Portfolio shed 10 fils to 1.210 dinars.

Industrials dominated on Sunday, with a 432,759 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.41 percent. Banks had a 376,790 dinar turnover and a similar index rise of 0.41 percent while services had a healthy 179,003 dinar turnover and an index rise of 0.01 percent.
A total of 379,137 shares worth 175,125 dinars changed hands in healthy trade in the parallel market. Of 19 shares traded, 8 advanced, four declined and seven were unchanged. One posted a year low.
